contents.html_ja: 2006年のその他の計画には、Digital Signature Standard（DSS）の改訂の完成、デジタル署名の生成と検証に必要な保証を得るための勧告、決定論的ランダムビット生成器（DRBG）を定める勧告があります。DRBG の勧告は、乱数生成に関する American National Standard を複数年・複数部にわたって策定する取り組みの一部です。
contents.html: Other plans for 2006 include the completion of a revision of the Digital Signature Standard (DSS), a recommendation for obtaining the required assurances for generating and verifying digital signatures, and a recommendation that specifies Deterministic Random Bit Generators (DRBGs). The DRBG recommendation is one part of the multi-year, multi-part development of a American National Standard for random number generation.

contents.html_ja: 生体認証技術は、生理的または行動的な特徴の認識に基づいて、人物を識別し、または人物の身元を検証する自動化された方法で構成されます。利用者は、標準ベースで相互運用可能な高性能の生体認証システムが、適時に開発されることを必要としています。オープンシステム標準の適時な策定がなければ、独自仕様のシステムからオープンシステム標準ベースのソリューションへの移行は、通常、より困難で費用がかかります。したがって、標準は当部門の生体認証プログラムの礎です。国土安全保障と ID 盗難防止のために新しい情報技術システムを展開するには、生体認証に関する国内および国際的な合意標準の両方が必要です。当部門は、正式な国内および国際的な生体認証標準と、それに関連する適合性評価の策定を加速することで、オープンシステム標準に対する政府と市場の要求に応えています。
contents.html: Biometric technologies consist of automated methods of identifying a person or verifying the identity of a person based upon recognition of a physiological or a behavioral characteristic. Consumers need biometric-based high-performance, interoperable (standards-based) systems developed in a timely fashion. In the absence of timely open systems standards developments, migration from proprietary systems to open-systems standard-based solutions is usually more difficult and expensive. Therefore, standards are the cornerstone of our biometrics program. Deploying new information technology systems for homeland security and for preventing ID theft require both national and international consensus standards for biometrics. We are responding to government and market requirements for open-system standards by accelerating development of formal national and international biometric standards and associated conformity assessments.

contents.html: These standards and associated conformity assessments need further development in order to help deploy significantly better, open-systems security solutions. We have identified the critical tasks that will help power the development of these standards so that the deployment of such systems may be accelerated. Consequently, in the past years we have worked in close partnership with other U.S. government agencies and U.S. industry to establish standards bodies for accelerating the development of formal national and international biometric standards of high relevance to the Nation. This program is a major catalyst for biometric standardization and adoption of biometric standards.
contents.html_ja: これらの標準と関連する適合性評価は、大幅により優れたオープンシステムのセキュリティソリューションの展開を助けるため、さらなる策定が必要です。そうしたシステムの展開を早められるよう、これらの標準の策定を後押しする重要なタスクを特定しました。その結果、ここ数年、当部門は他の米国政府機関および米国産業界と緊密に連携して、国にとって関連性の高い、正式な国内および国際的な生体認証標準の策定を加速するための標準化団体を設立してきました。このプログラムは、生体認証の標準化と、生体認証標準の採用の大きな促進役です。

contents.html_ja: 国内では、NIST 情報技術研究所（ITL）の生体認証標準プログラムが、InterNational Committee for Information Technology Standards（INCITS）のもとの Technical Committee M1 の設立を支援しました。INCITS M1 の目的は、正式な国内および国際的な汎用の生体認証標準を迅速に策定し承認するための、米国における優先度が高く重点を絞った包括的な取り組みを確実にすることです。これらの標準は、国土防衛、ID 窃取の防止、生体認証による個人認証に基づくその他の政府や商用の用途など、米国のニーズにとって重要と考えられています。NIST は、この標準策定団体に積極的に技術面で貢献しており、その標準策定プロジェクトのいくつかを後援してきました。CSD のプログラム専門家は、ITL の Information Access Division（IAD）の生体認証の専門家と緊密に協力しています。2004年と2005年に、INCITS M1 は、顔認識、指画像、指のマニューシャ、指紋パターン、虹彩認識、手形状、署名／サインなど、さまざまな生体認証モダリティ向けの生体データ交換標準を数多く承認しました。INCITS M1 は現在、これらの生体データ交換形式の複数について、適合性試験方法論の標準を策定しています。2005年に、INCITS M1 は、生体認証の性能試験と報告を定める複数部構成の標準のうち、3 つの部の策定を完了しました。INCITS M1 はまた、2 つの生体認証アプリケーションプロファイル、Verification & Identification of Transportation Workers と Biometric-Based Personal Identification for Border Management も承認しました。生体データ交換形式の適合性試験方法論の策定に加えて、NIST は、他の INCITS M1 の構成員とともに、BioAPI 仕様の適合性試験方法論標準の策定を共同で後援しました。INCITS M1 は現在、マルチ生体認証と生体認証フュージョンデータを支える標準、生体サンプルの品質標準、データ交換形式標準の生体認証性能と相互運用性の試験を定める標準の策定にも取り組んでいます。NIST の専門家は、これらの標準策定に非常に積極的に関わっています。
contents.html: Nationally, NIST’s Information Technology Laboratory’s (ITL’s) biometric standards program helped to establish Technical Committee M1 under the InterNational Committee for Information Technology Standards (INCITS). The purpose of INCITS M1 is to ensure a high-priority, focused and comprehensive approach in the U.S. for the rapid development and approval of formal national and international generic biometric standards. These standards are considered to be critical for U.S. needs, such as homeland defense, the prevention of identity theft and for other government and commercial applications based on biometric personal authentication. NIST is an active technical contributor to this standards development body and has sponsored several of their standards development projects. The program experts from CSD work in close collaboration with ITL’s Information Access Division’s (IAD’s) biometric experts. During 2004 and 2005, INCITS M1 approved a number of biometric data interchange standards for different biometric modalities (face recognition, finger image, finger minutiae, finger pattern, iris recognition, hand geometry, and signature/sign). INCITS M1 is currently developing conformance testing methodology standards for a number of these biometric data interchange formats. In 2005 INCITS M1 completed the development of three parts of a multipart standard that specifies biometric performance testing and reporting. INCITS M1 also approved two biometric application profiles: Verification & Identification of Transportation Workers and Biometric-Based Personal Identification for Border Management. In addition to the development of conformance testing methodologies for biometric data interchange formats, NIST co-sponsored with other INCITS M1 members, the development of a conformance testing methodology standard for the BioAPI specification. INCITS M1 is currently addressing the development of standards to support multi-biometrics and biometric fusion data, a biometric sample quality standard, and a standard to specify biometric performance and interoperability testing of data interchange format standards. NIST experts are very active in these standards developments.

contents.html: Internationally, we successfully supported the establishment of the International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission Joint Technical Committee 1 Subcommittee 37-Biometrics (ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 37-Biometrics). INCITS M1 is the national Technical Committee responsible for representing the U.S. in JTC1/SC 37. We provide the chairperson for these two standards bodies and manage their standards programs.We provide the chair of the national standards development efforts on biometric profiles (the Convener of the JTC 1/SC 37 Working Group responsible for the international biometric profile projects is provided by ITL). A large number of the projects within JTC 1 SC 37’s program of work were initiated by the U.S. (through INCITS M1). During 2005, JTC 1/SC 37 approved four of these standards. They specify biometric data interchange standard formats for face recognition (face image), finger minutiae, finger image and iris recognition (iris image). ISO published these standards also during 2005. Six additional standards are scheduled to be approved by JTC 1/SC 37 in the first quarter of 2006. NIST experts are also very active in the development of JTC 1/SC 37’s standards portfolio. We are involved in ongoing efforts within JTC 1/SC37 in defining a taxonomy to enable the Subcommittee to determine the issues that need to be resolved to ensure that conformance, interoperability, performance, and quality for the biometric data interchange format standards can be adequately addressed.
contents.html_ja: 国際的には、国際標準化機構／国際電気標準会議の合同技術委員会1の小委員会37（生体認証）（ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 37-Biometrics）の設立を成功裏に支援しました。INCITS M1 は、JTC1/SC 37 で米国を代表する責任を担う国内技術委員会です。NIST は、これら2つの標準化団体の議長を務め、その標準化プログラムを管理しています。NIST は、生体認証プロファイルに関する国内標準策定の取り組みでも議長を務めています（国際的な生体認証プロファイルのプロジェクトを担当する JTC 1/SC 37 作業部会の招集者は ITL が務めています）。JTC 1 SC 37 の作業計画にある多数のプロジェクトは、米国が（INCITS M1 を通じて）開始しました。2005年に、JTC 1/SC 37 はこれらの標準のうち4つを承認しました。これらは、顔認識（顔画像）、指のマニューシャ、指画像、虹彩認識（虹彩画像）の生体データ交換標準形式を定めています。ISO もこれらの標準を2005年中に発行しました。さらに6つの標準が、2006年の第1四半期に JTC 1/SC 37 で承認される予定です。NIST の専門家は、JTC 1/SC 37 の標準群の策定にも非常に積極的に関わっています。生体データ交換形式標準の適合性、相互運用性、性能、品質に適切に対処するために解決すべき課題を小委員会が判断できるようにする分類体系の定義について、NIST は JTC 1/SC37 内で続けられている取り組みに関わっています。

contents.html_ja: INCITS M1 と JTC 1/SC 37 で策定中の生体認証標準は、相互運用性とデータ交換を支えます。いずれかの生体データ交換形式（いずれかの生体認証モダリティ）に適合する Biometric Service Provider は、これらの標準のいずれかに適合するデータ構造を作成し、解釈できます。適合のための要件は、生体データ形式交換標準のいずれかに適合する生体データを、CBEFF（Common Biometric Exchange Formats Framework）に適合するデータ構造の中に埋め込むことです。BioAPI は、幅広い生体認証技術と連携するための汎用的な方法を定義しています。BioAPI で定義されるデータ構造は、CBEFF の具体化です。BSP は BioAPI に適合すると見込まれています。アプリケーションは、BioAPI、CBEFF、策定中の生体認証プロファイルのいずれかに適合すると見込まれています。
contents.html: Biometric standards under development in INCITS M1 and JTC 1/SC 37 support interoperability and data interchange. Biometric Service Providers conforming to one of the biometric data interchange formats (any one of the biometric modalities) can develop and interpret a data structure that conforms to one of these standards. A requirement for conformance is embedding the biometric data that conforms to one of the biometric data format interchange standards within a data structure that conforms to CBEFF (Common Biometric Exchange Formats Framework). BioAPI defines a generic way of interfacing to a broad range of biometric technologies. The data structure defined in BioAPI is an instantiation of CBEFF. BSPs are expected to conform to BioAPI. Applications are expected to conform to BioAPI, CBEFF and one of the biometric profiles under development.

contents.html: In 2004, the International Civil Aviation Administration (ICAO) adopted a global, harmonized blueprint for the integration of biometric identification information into passports. The biometric requirements include the use of facial recognition as the globally interoperable biometric for travel documents; the use of fingerprint in its several differing technical formulations; and the use of iris as well. ICAO directly adopted the SC 37 standards for its applications. The ICAO community has also committed conformance to and adoption of CBEFF as the data structure for the utilization of biometrics for global interoperability and standardization. ICAO requires conformance to the standards developed by JTC 1/SC 37 for these biometric data interchange standard formats and CBEFF.
contents.html_ja: 2004年に、International Civil Aviation Administration（ICAO）は、生体識別情報をパスポートに組み込むための、世界的に調和した青写真を採用しました。生体認証の要件には、渡航文書で世界的に相互運用可能な生体情報としての顔認識の使用、いくつかの異なる技術的定式化による指紋の使用、虹彩の使用も含まれます。ICAO は、SC 37 の標準を自らのアプリケーションに直接採用しました。ICAO のコミュニティは、世界的な相互運用性と標準化のための生体情報の利用におけるデータ構造として、CBEFF への適合と採用も約束しました。ICAO は、これらの生体データ交換標準形式と CBEFF について、JTC 1/SC 37 が策定した標準への適合を求めています。

contents.html_ja: 国連の International Labour Office（ILO）は、バーコードに指紋テンプレートを含む Seafarers Identity Document（SID）を定める Convention 185 を承認しました。2004年3月に、ILO の理事会は、JTC1/SC 37 のいくつかのドラフト標準の使用を定める Technical Report を承認しました。ILO が規範として指定している JTC 1/SC 37 の具体的なデータ交換標準は、指のマニューシャと指画像のデータ交換形式です。これは、ISO の外部の機関が、国際条約で JTC 1/SC 37 の標準の使用を明確に義務づけた初めての例です。
contents.html: The International Labour Office of the United Nations (ILO) has approved Convention 185, which defines a Seafarers Identity Document (SID) containing fingerprint templates in a barcode. In March 2004, the ILO governing body approved a Technical Report that specifies the use of several JTC1/SC 37 draft standards. The specific JTC 1/SC 37 data interchange standards being specified as normative by the ILO are the finger minutiae and finger image data interchange formats. This represents the first time an external agency to ISO has specifically mandated the use of JTC 1/SC 37 standards in an international treaty.

contents.html_ja: 国内では、2004年10月に、DHS は、INCITS M1 が策定した顔認識標準を採用し、この標準の一部を抽出して、プロジェクト管理者、ソフトウェア・システム開発者、撮影者と被写体を含む DHS の特定の利用者向けのガイドラインを提供し、統一された写真（ポスター）を作成するためのベストプラクティスを策定しました。さらに、DHS の Transportation Worker Identification Credential（TWIC）Program（立会いなしの物理的またはロジカルなアクセスを必要とするすべての要員が使う、システム全体の共通クレデンシャル）のフェーズ III（プロトタイプフェーズ）には、生体認証プロファイル Verification & Identification of Transportation Workers を含む、該当する INCITS M1 標準への要件が含まれています。Greater Orlando Aviation Authority（GOAA）が運営する DHS/TSA の Registered Traveler Program のサブパイロットは、INCITS M1 の 2 つのインタフェース標準である BioAPI 仕様と CBEFF、および INCITS M1 が策定した生体データ交換標準の一部を求めています。CBEFF は、CSD の専門家と国家安全保障局（NSA）の主導のもと、当初 NIST IR 6529-A として発行されました。ドラフト特別刊行物（SP）800-76、Biometric Data Specification for Personal Identity Verification は、ドラフト SP で定める生体データを CBEFF 構造で包むことを求めています。
contents.html: Nationally, in October 2004, DHS adopted the face recognition standard developed by INCITS M1 in order to extract portions of this standard to provide guidelines for specific DHS users including project managers, software and system developers, photographers and subjects, and to develop best practices for producing uniform photographs (posters). In addition, Phase III— Prototype Phase of DHS’s Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) Program (a system-wide common credential to be used for all personnel requiring unescorted physical and/or logical access), includes requirements to the INCITS M1 standards, as applicable, including the Biometric profile—Verification & Identification of Transportation Workers. A sub-pilot of the DHS/TSA registered Traveler Program administered by the Greater Orlando Aviation Authority (GOAA) requires two INCITS M1 interface standards, the BioAPI Specification, and the CBEFF, and some of the biometric data interchange standards developed by INCITS M1. CBEFF was originally published as NIST IR 6529-A under the leadership of CSD experts and the National Security Agency (NSA). Draft Special Publication (SP) 800-76, Biometric Data Specification for Personal Identity Verification, requires wrapping the biometric data specified in the draft SP in a CBEFF structure.

contents.html_ja: 生体認証のインキュベーターとみなされている BC は、生体認証に関する米国政府の窓口の役割を果たしています。現在、60 を超える機関、産業界、学術界を代表する 900 人を超える会員がいます。NIST は、NSA とともに BC の共同議長を務めています。BC は、年次会議、技術ワークショップ、生体認証の技術開発を後援しています。NIST と BC が後援する NIST/BC Biometric Working Group は、ここ数年、政府の利用者や産業界とともに生体認証の仕様を策定してきました。過去には、国内標準と国際標準としてさらに処理するため、(1) Biometric Data Protection and Usage、(2) Biometric Application Programming Interface for Java Card、(3) CBEFF の拡張版の 3 つの仕様を承認し、正式な標準化団体に提供しました。CBEFF の国際版は、JTC 1/SC 37 内で策定されています。CBEFF は、INCITS M1 と JTC 1/SC 37 内で策定中の国内および国際的なデータ交換標準にとって、適合のための要件です。
contents.html: The BC, which is considered to be a biometrics incubator, serves as a U.S. government focal point for biometrics. It currently consists of over 900 members representing over 60 agencies, industry and academe. NIST co-chairs the BC with NSA. The BC sponsors an annual conference, technical workshops and biometrics technical developments. The NIST/BC Biometric Working Group, sponsored by NIST and the BC has been working in the last few years with government users and industry developing biometric specifications. In the past it approved and provided to formal standards bodies three specifications for further processing as national and international standards, including (1) Biometric Data Protection and Usage, (2) Biometric Application Programming Interface for Java Card, and (3) an augmented version of CBEFF. An international version of CBEFF is being developed within JTC 1/SC 37. CBEFF is a requirement for conformance for the national and international data interchange standards under development within INCITS M1 and JTC 1/SC 37.

contents.html_ja: NIST は、BioAPI Consortium とその運営委員会の構成員でもあります。BioAPI Consortium の会員は、生体認証ベンダー、エンドユーザー、システム開発者、相手先ブランド製造業者（OEM）を含む 100 を超える組織で構成されています。このコンソーシアムは、INCITS 358-2002 として承認された BioAPI 仕様を策定しました。BioAPI 仕様と関連標準は、JTC 1/SC 37 で策定中です。BioAPI は、国際標準化機構（ISO）標準の候補です。2006年の第 1 四半期に ISO 標準として承認される見込みです。
contents.html: NIST is also a member of the BioAPI Consortium and its Steering Committee. BioAPI Consortium’s membership consists of over 100 organizations, including biometric vendors, end-users, system developers and original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). This consortium developed the BioAPI specification, which was approved as INCITS 358-2002. The BioAPI specification and related standards are under development in JTC 1/SC 37. BioAPI is an International Organization of Standardization (ISO) standard candidate. It is expected to be approved as an ISO standard during the 1 st Quarter of 2006.

contents.html_ja: 2005年に、NIST は、BioAPI 仕様の国内版に対する適合性試験スイート（CTS）の実装と、INCITS M1 のもとでの文書規格の策定を主導しました。この規格プロジェクトは、NIST/ITL/CSD、国防総省 Biometrics Management Office（BMO）、National Biometric Security Project（NBSP）、Saflink Corporation、The Biometric Foundation（TBF）が後援しました。最初の CTS 実装は、適合性試験方法論規格のドラフトで定められた概念と原則を用いて開発されました。最初の CTS 実装は NBSP が共同で後援し、Saflink Corporation が開発しました。NIST/ITL/CSD と連携して、国防総省 BMO は BioAPI CTS の同様の実装を独自に開発してきました。これらの試験ツールは、BioAPI 標準への適合をすでに求めている、または近い将来求めることに関心を持つ政府機関内の利用者、BioAPI 標準およびその他の新たな標準への適合を検証する適合性評価プログラムの設立の可能性、ならびに利用者向けに提供されるものと同じ試験ツールを使って、任意の合意標準に適合する製品を開発することに関心を持つ製品開発者を支援するために開発されています。NIST と国防総省 BMO は現在、これらのツールが一般に公開される前に、BioAPI 標準への適合を主張する複数ベンダーの BSP を用いて試験結果を相互検証するため、これらの CTS の初期版を集中的に試験しています。試験は、The Biometric Foundation（これも NBSP が共同で後援）の専門家と協力して実施しています。2006年には、他の文書規格や仕様を支えるため、適合性試験スイート開発の取り組みを拡大する計画です。CBEFF に適合する生体データ構造の実装を試験する CTS も計画されています。
contents.html: During 2005 NIST has led an effort to develop an implementation of a conformance testing suite (CTS) for the national version of the BioAPI specification as well as the development of a documentary standard under INCITS M1. This standard project was sponsored by NIST/ITL/CSD, DoD Biometrics Management Office (BMO), the National Biometric Security Project (NBSP), Saflink Corporation, and The Biometric Foundation (TBF). The initial CTS implementation was developed using concepts and principles specified in the draft conformance testing methodology standard. The initial CTS implementation was co-sponsored by NBSP and developed by Saflink Corporation. In coordination with NIST/ITL/CSD, DoD BMO has been independently developing a similar implementation of the BioAPI CTS. These test tools are being developed in support of users within Government Agencies already requiring, or interested in requiring in the near future, that Biometric Service Providers (BSPs) conform to the BioAPI standard; the possible establishment of conformity assessment programs to validate conformance to the BioAPI standard and other emerging standards; and product developers interested in developing products conforming to voluntary consensus biometric standards by using the same test tools available to users. NIST and DoD BMO are currently performing intensive testing of the initial versions of these CTSs in order to cross - validate the test results using a number of vendor BSPs claiming conformance to the BioAPI standard before anticipated release of these tools to the public. Our tests are performed in cooperation with experts from The Biometric Foundation (also co-sponsored by NBSP). We are planning to extend conformance test suite development efforts during 2006 in support of other documentary standards and specifications. CTSs to test implementation of biometric data structures conforming to CBEFF are planned.

contents.html: e-AUTHENTICATION

contents.html_ja: 行政管理予算局（OMB）は、利用者の遠隔識別、すなわち電子認証を、インターネットベースの政府サービスの提供に対する、分野横断的な障害として特定しました。電子政府の利点を十分に実現するには、政府機関に、政府のシステムとデータの保護に合わせた電子認証の方針と、それに対応する技術ガイダンスが必要です。このプロジェクトは、米国政府内の電子認証の方針構造を確立し、連邦機関全体で電子認証が一貫して実施されるよう促進します。この一貫性は、電子政府アプリケーションを通じてより多くの取引を行うために必要な電子的プロセスを保護することで、政府の効率を高めるのにも役立ちます。
contents.html: The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) has identified the remote identification of users, or e-authentication, as a crosscutting impediment to the provision of Internet-based government services. To fully realize the benefits of electronic government, government agencies require e-authentication policies and corresponding technical guidance tailored to the protection of government systems and data. This project establishes a policy structure for e-authentication within the U.S. government, promoting consistent implementation of e-authentication across Federal agencies. This consistency will in turn help to enhance government efficiency by securing electronic processes needed to conduct more transactions through e-government applications.

contents.html_ja: OMB は、2003年12月に、覚書 M-04-04、E-Authentication Guidance for Federal Agencies を公開しました。この OMB の方針覚書は、主張された ID が有効であるという保証の観点から、認証の 4 つのレベル、すなわちレベル 1 から 4 を定義しました。OMB のガイダンスは、認証の誤りが起こりうる結果に基づいて、アプリケーションに適した認証レベルを判断するため、機関にリスク評価を行うことを求めています。これは、たとえば利用者がより機微な個人情報にアクセスできるようなシステムなど、レベル 4 の認証を使うシステムでは、利用者の身元が主張どおりであることに対する保証がはるかに高いことを意味します。リスク評価を完了し、特定したリスクを必要な保証レベルに対応付けた後、OMB のガイダンスは、機関に対し、NIST の技術ガイダンスに基づいて適切な認証の仕組みを特定し、実装するよう指示しています。
contents.html: OMB released memorandum M-04-04, E-Authentication Guidance for Federal Agencies, in December 2003. This OMB policy memorandum defined four levels of authentication – Levels 1 to 4 – in terms of the assurance that an asserted identity is valid. The OMB guidance requires agencies to perform a risk assessment to determine the appropriate authentication level for an application based on the likely consequences of an authentication error. This means a system using Level 4 authentication – a system that allows a user access to more sensitive, personal information for example – has a much higher assurance that a user's identity is what it is claimed it to be. After completing a risk assessment and mapping the identified risks to the required assurance level, OMB guidance directs agencies to identify and implement appropriate authentication mechanisms based on NIST technical guidance.

contents.html_ja: 2004年に、当部門の電子認証の技術ガイダンスが、SP 800-63、Recommendation for Electronic Authentication として発行されました。この勧告は、電子認証を実装する機関に、個人が連邦 IT システムに対して自らの身元を遠隔で認証できるようにする方法についての技術ガイダンスを提供します。SP 800-63 は、身元確認と登録、トークン、遠隔認証の仕組み、アサーションの仕組みの分野について、4 つの保証レベルのそれぞれに対する具体的な技術要件を述べています。扱うのは、個人に暗号鍵やパスワードなどのシークレットの所持と管理を実証させることで機能する認証の仕組みのみです。
contents.html: In 2004, our e-authentication technical guidance was published as SP 800-63, Recommendation for Electronic Authentication. This recommendation provides technical guidance to agencies implementing electronic authentication on how to allow an individual person to remotely authenticate his or her identity to a Federal IT system. SP 800-63 states specific technical requirements for each of the four levels of assurance in the areas of identity proofing and registration, tokens, remote authentication mechanisms and assertion mechanisms. It only addresses authentication mechanisms that work by making the individual demonstrate possession and control of a secret, such as a cryptographic key or a password.

contents.html_ja: 2005年には、知識ベース認証（KBA）や生体認証など、電子認証を支えるために使える他の技術を調査しました。KBA は、個人が主張する身元を遠隔で検証する手段として、その個人の知識を確かめる一連の技法を指します。KBA は、連邦機関や企業との電子的な取引をまれにしか行わない個人を遠隔で認証するのに特に有用なツールですが、この情報は非公開であっても実際には秘密ではないため、個人の身元に対する信頼を得るのは難しい場合があります。こうした課題に対応するため、OMB の保証レベル1および2を満たす KBA の技術要件を示し、汎用的な KBA モデルを定義するホワイトペーパーを作成しました。2006年には、このガイダンスを SP 800-63 に取り入れます。生体認証の方法は、たとえば建物への入場のように、認証地点に物理的にいる個人を認証するために広く使われています。生体情報は、SP 800-63 が扱う従来の遠隔認証プロトコルで使うのに適した秘密ではありません。ローカル認証の場合、請求者は検証者が管理する取得装置を使うため、認証に生体情報を秘密にしておく必要はありません。2005年には、遠隔認証プロトコルと生体認証を検討するワークショップを開催しました。ワークショップの結果に基づき、CSD は産業界と協力し、オープンネットワーク上での個人の遠隔認証における生体認証の役割を引き続き調査するため、International Committee for Information Technology Standards（INCITS）M1 Ad Hoc グループの設立を支援しました。このグループは、2006年に調査結果に関する技術報告書を提供する予定です。
contents.html: In 2005, we studied other technologies that could be used to support electronic authentication including knowledge based authentication (KBA) and biometrics. KBA refers to a class of techniques for testing the personal knowledge of an individual as a way to remotely verify the individual’s claimed identity. KBA is a particularly useful tool to remotely authenticate individuals who conduct business electronically with Federal agencies or businesses infrequently; however, since this information is private but not actually secret, confidence in the identity of an individual may be hard to achieve. To meet these challenges, we developed a white paper that defines a generic KBA model and identifies the KBA technical requirements state satisfy OMB assurances Levels 1 and 2. In 2006, we will incorporate this guidance into the SP 800-63. Biometric methods are widely used to authenticate individuals who are physically present at the authentication point, for example, for entry into buildings. Biometrics do not constitute secrets suitable for use in the conventional remote authentication protocols addressed in SP 800-63. In the local authentication case, the claimant uses a capture device controlled by the verifier, so authentication does not require that biometrics be kept secret. In 2005, we held a workshop to examine remote authentication protocols and biometrics. Based on the results of the workshop, CSD, in collaboration with industry, helped form the International Committee for Information Technology Standards (INCITS) M1 Ad Hoc group to continue studying the role of biometrics in the remote authentication of individuals across open networks. This group will provide a technical report on its findings in 2006.

contents.html_ja: 電子認証の技法を実装する個々の政府機関が、多数の機関とアプリケーションにまたがる包括的なインフラを使わず、アプリケーションごとに個別の技法を実装すると、法外な費用がかかります。また、国民が政府とやり取りする際に、複数のクレデンシャルを維持しなければならず、それらのクレデンシャルでは必要なサービスにアクセスできないという負担もあります。機関間で相互運用可能なインフラという取り組み方が、より優れた選択肢であることは明らかです。
contents.html: Individual government agencies implementing electronic authentication techniques would incur prohibitive costs if they were to implement separate techniques for each application instead of an umbrella infrastructure that could span numerous agencies and applications. There is also a burden on the public in interacting with the government by having to maintain multiple credentials and not being able to access the services they need using those credentials. It is clear that a cross-agency interoperable infrastructure approach is a better alternative.

contents.html_ja: OMB は、2002年電子政府法に基づく責任に従って、2006会計年度から、公開鍵基盤（PKI）サービスの利用を予定する連邦機関は、独自の内部 PKI を確立するのではなく、Federal Common Policy Framework のもとで運営される、適格なマネージドサービス提供者である Shared Service Provider（SSP）からそれを購入することと決定しました。Common Policy Framework は、2004年に当部門が策定した一連の統一ポリシーです。
contents.html: Pursuant to its responsibilities under the Electronic Government Act of 2002, OMB has determined that beginning in fiscal year 2006 Federal agencies that intend to use Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) services will be buying them from qualified managed service providers – Shared Service Providers (SSPs) – operating under the Federal Common Policy Framework rather than establishing their own internal PKI. The Common Policy Framework is a suite of uniform policies developed by us in 2004.

contents.html_ja: 連邦ブリッジ認証局と相互認証された PKI 運用を持つ機関は、これらの新しいマネージドサービス提供者への移行を求められませんが、時間が経つにつれて、これらの新しい提供者への移行が望ましくなる場合があります。この 2 段階のプロセスは、産業界と政府の両方に費用の節約をもたらします。第一に、各機関が独自の特殊なポリシーを策定するのではなく、共通のポリシーを満たすよう PKI サービスが開発されることを確実にし、第二に、連邦機関（および一般調達局（GSA）Schedules のその他の認可された利用者）が、タスクオーダーとデリバリーオーダーを出せる共通の契約を持つことによってです。
contents.html: Agencies with PKI operations that are cross-certified with the Federal Bridge Certification Authority will not be required to migrate to these new managed service providers, but as time goes on it may become desirable to migrate to these new providers. This two-step process will result in cost savings to both industry and government; first by insuring that PKI services are developed to meet a common policy, rather than having each agency developing its own idiosyncratic policy, and secondly by having a common contract against which task and delivery orders may be placed by Federal agencies (and other authorized users of the General Services Administration (GSA) Schedules).

contents.html_ja: 当部門は、連邦 PKI の開発と展開を引き続き支援しています。連邦 PKI の証明書ポリシー群と連邦ブリッジ認証局の運用を管理する Federal PKI Policy Authority の副議長を提供しています。また、Internet Engineering Task Force（IETF）の PKI Working Group の共同議長を務め、関連する Path Validation Testing を管理しています。これらの活動は、すべてのインターネット利用者のための相互運用可能なインフラを前進させます。
contents.html: We continue to support the development and deployment of the Federal PKI. We provide the vice-chair of the Federal PKI Policy Authority, which manages the suite of Federal PKI Certificate Policies and the operations of the Federal Bridge Certification Authority. We also co-chair the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) PKI Working Group and is managing the related Path Validation Testing. These activities advance interoperable infrastructures for all Internet users.

contents.html_ja: 当部門は、Federal Identity Credential Committee の SSP Subcommittee で主導的な役割を果たしています。FICC と SSP プログラムを推進する技術的知識と専門性を提供しています。また、SSP Subcommittee の構成員を複数出しており、同小委員会の文書ライブラリの策定にも大きく貢献してきました。
contents.html: We play a leading role on the Federal Identity Credential Committee’s SSP Subcommittee. We provide the technical knowledge and expertise that drive the FICC and the SSP Program. We also provide several members of the SSP Subcommittee and have contributed heavily to the development of the Subcommittee’s library of documents.

contents.html_ja: SSP の候補は、Common Policy Framework で定められた要件を満たし、連邦の認証と認定の要件を満たさなければなりません。SSP になることを望む PKI サービスのベンダーは、SSP Subcommittee が定めた客観的な要件の一覧を満たさなければなりません。SSP Subcommittee は、承認された 3 つの PKI 提供者の最初の一覧を確立する際に、この要件の一覧を用いて、ベンダーの運用手順を評価し、第三者監査をレビューし、運用上の準拠を実証する内容を評価しました。
contents.html: Potential SSPs must meet the requirements established in the Common Policy Framework and satisfy the Federal certification and accreditation requirements. Vendors of PKI services wishing to be an SSP must meet an objective list of requirements established by the SSP Subcommittee. The SSP Subcommittee used this list of requirements to evaluate vendors’ operational procedures, review third-party audits and assess operational compliance demonstrations when establishing the initial list of three approved PKI providers.

contents.html: CSD, as part of the SSP Subcommittee, has developed the Shared Service Provider Roadmap. The Shared Service Provider Roadmap is intended to identify the background information, phases and activities related to the selection process for prospective PKI managed service providers. This document identifies the process by which a vendor qualifies for inclusion on the Qualified Bidders List. The document also describes requirements that must be met to maintain qualification, as well as contracting considerations.
contents.html_ja: CSD は、SSP Subcommittee の一員として、Shared Service Provider Roadmap を策定しました。Shared Service Provider Roadmap は、PKI マネージドサービス提供者の候補を選定するプロセスに関連する背景情報、フェーズ、活動を特定することを意図しています。この文書は、ベンダーが Qualified Bidders List への掲載資格を得るプロセスを特定しています。また、この文書は、資格を維持するために満たさなければならない要件と、契約上の考慮事項も記述しています。

contents.html_ja: 当部門はまた、GSA によるオンライン電子認証クレデンシャル検証インフラの開発も支援しています。GSA の e-Authentication Gateway は、政府のアプリケーションと非政府の CSP を仲介し、アプリケーションがさまざまな身分証明クレデンシャルを受け入れられるようにします。たとえば、個人は、銀行と確立したパスワードなどの認証の仕組みを、政府のアプリケーションへのアクセスに活用できる場合があります。GSA E-Authentication Gateway のアーキテクチャは、CSP や政府のアプリケーションと認証情報を交換するために、SAML、TLS、PKI に依拠しています。CSD は、E-Authentication Gateway、CSP、政府のアプリケーションの間で、TLS で保護された認証情報の送信を支える PKI アーキテクチャと PKI ポリシーを策定して、GSA を支援しました。
contents.html: We are also assisting GSA in the development of an online e-authentication credential validation infrastructure. The GSA e-Authentication Gateway mediates between government applications and non-government CSPs, permitting applications to accept a variety of identification credentials. For example, individuals may be able to leverage authentication mechanisms, such as passwords, established with their banks to access government applications. The GSA E-Authentication Gateway architecture relies on SAML, TLS, and PKI to exchange authentication information with CSPs and government applications. CSD assisted GSA by developing PKI architecture and PKI policies supporting TLS-protected transmission of authentication information between the E-Authentication Gateway, CSPs and government applications.

contents.html_ja: 2002年に、議会は、米国全土の投票機器のアップグレードを促すために Help America Vote Act（HAVA）を可決しました。HAVA は、Election Assistance Commission（EAC）と、国立標準技術研究所（NIST）所長が議長を務める Technical Guidelines Development Committee（TGDC）を設置しました。HAVA は、NIST に対し、ヒューマンファクター、セキュリティ、試験所認定に関する取り組みで、EAC と TGDC に技術的支援を提供するよう求めています。投票システムのセキュリティと透明性に関する問題を調査・研究するため、TGDC は Security and Transparency Subcommittee（STS）を設置しました。当部門は、投票機器のセキュリティに関する EAC、TGDC、STS の活動を支援しています。
contents.html: In 2002, Congress passed the Help America Vote Act (HAVA) to encourage the upgrade of voting equipment across the United States. HAVA established the Election Assistance Commission (EAC) and the Technical Guidelines Development Committee (TGDC), chaired by the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). HAVA calls on NIST to provide technical support to the EAC and TGDC in efforts related to human factors, security, and laboratory accreditation. To explore and research issues related to the security and transparency of voting systems, the TGDC established the Security and Transparency Subcommittee (STS). We support the activities of the EAC, TGDC, and STS related to voting equipment security.

contents.html_ja: 昨年は、Voluntary Voting System Guidelines（VVSG）が更新され、安全なソフトウェアの配布、セットアップの検証、有権者が検証できる紙の監査証跡（VVPAT）、無線技術の安全な使用を扱う新しい節が加わりました。更新された VVSG では、Independent Dual Verification（IDV）の概念が導入されました。その目的は、非常に高い精度で正しさを監査できる投票記録の作成です。
contents.html: In the past year, the Voluntary Voting System Guidelines (VVSG) were updated with new sections covering secure software distribution, setup validation, voter verified paper audit trail (VVPAT), and secure use of wireless technology. The concept of Independent Dual Verification (IDV) was introduced in the updated VVSG where the objective is the production of ballot records whose correctness can be audited to very high levels of precision.

contents.html_ja: 2006年の計画には、投票システムの脅威分析ワークショップの開催、TGDC の全体会合の主催、STS の活動の支援、EAC および TGDC と協力した VVSG の大幅な改訂と再構成、投票システムのセキュリティと透明性を高める方法を探るための、投票システムのベンダー、州の選挙管理官、学術界との関わりがあります。
contents.html: Plans for 2006 include holding a threat analysis workshop for voting systems, hosting the TGDC plenary meetings, supporting STS activities, working with the EAC and TGDC to substantially revise and restructure the VVSG, engaging the voting system vendor, state election official, and academic communities to explore ways to increase voting system security and transparency.

contents.html_ja: Bronze Medal Award は、同研究所が授与できる最高の名誉ある表彰です。所長が承認するこの賞は、より有効で効率的な管理システムをもたらした業務に加え、方法と手順の開発と改善における並外れた主体性や創造力の発揮を称えるものです。また、主要プログラムに影響を与える重要な貢献、同研究所内の科学的業績、少なくとも 5 年連続での割り当てられたタスクの優れた遂行に対しても授与されます。
contents.html: The Bronze Medal Award is the highest honorary recognition available for Institute presentation. The award, approved by the Director, recognizes work that has resulted in more effective and efficient management systems as well as the demonstration of unusual initiative or creative ability in the development and improvement of methods and procedures. It also is given for significant contribution affecting major programs, scientific accomplishment within the Institute, and superior performance of assigned tasks for at least five consecutive years.

contents.html: Mr. Timothy Grance and Ms. Joan Hash are recognized for their efforts in providing standards and guidelines in support of Federal Information Security Programs and improving the management and technical processes that are essential to successful information security program implementation. Their work has been key in advancing overall security management and implementation strategy government-wide, nationally, and internationally, resulting in increased protection of information assets and supporting information technology infrastructures needed to provide critical public service.

contents.html_ja: IEEE Haraden Pratt Award は、IEEE の名誉理事であり、同協会に献身的で傑出した奉仕を行った Haraden Pratt を称えて、1971年に設けられました。会長、会計担当、続いて幹事を 23 年連続で務めた彼の、名誉理事を含む理事会での奉仕は、合計 31 年に及びました。この賞の目的は、同協会に傑出した奉仕を行った個人を称えることです。
contents.html: The IEEE Haraden Pratt Award was established in 1971 in honor of Haraden Pratt, who was Director Emeritus of the IEEE and who had given dedicated and distinguished service to the Institute. As President, Treasurer, and then Secretary for 23 consecutive years, his service on the Board of Directors, including that of Director Emeritus, totaled 31 years. The purpose of this award is to recognize individuals who have rendered outstanding service to the Institute.

contents.html_ja: NIST は、さまざまな方法で産業界と学術界の研究に資金を提供しています。Advanced Technology Program は、産業界と共同で、高リスク・高リターンのプロジェクトに共同出資しています。Small Business Innovation Research Program は、中小企業からの研究開発の提案に資金を提供しています。また、精密測定、火災研究、材料科学といった特定の分野での取り組みを奨励するため、その他の助成金も提供しています。産業界、学術界、その他の機関での研究を支援する助成金・賞は、同研究所の複数の部署を通じて、競争方式で提供されています。NIST の助成金プログラムの一般情報については、Ms. Joyce Brigham、(301) 975-6329、joyce.brigham@nist.gov にお問い合わせください。
contents.html: NIST funds industrial and academic research in a variety of ways. Our Advanced Technology Program co-funds high-risk, high-payoff projects with industry. The Small Business Innovation Research Program funds R&D proposals from small businesses. We also offer other grants to encourage work in specific fields: precision measurement, fire research and materials science. Grants/awards supporting research at industry, academic and other institutions are available on a competitive basis through several different Institute offices. For general information on NIST grants programs, contact Ms. Joyce Brigham, (301) 975-6329, joyce.brigham@nist.gov.

contents.html: Here’s your chance to satisfy that curiosity by spending part of your summer working elbow-to-elbow with researchers at NIST, one of the world’s leading research organizations and home to two Nobel Prize winners. Gain valuable hands-on experience, work with cutting-edge technology, meet peers from across the Nation (from San Francisco to Puerto Rico, New York to New Mexico), and sample the Washington, D.C., area. And, get paid while you're learning. For further information, see http://www.surf.nist.gov, or contact NIST SURF Program, 100 Bureau Dr., Stop 8400, Gaithersburg, MD 20899-8499, (301) 975-4200, NIST_SURF_program@nist.gov.

VERIFICATION

Authentication of an individual’s identity is a fundamental component of physical and logical access control processes. When individ-uals attempt to access security-sensitive build-ings, computer systems, or data, an access control decision must be made. An accurate determination of identity is an important component in making sound access control decisions.

A wide range of mechanisms is employed to authenticate identity, leveraging many different classes of identification identity credentials. For physical access, individual identity has tradition-ally been authenticated by use of paper creden-tials, such as driver’s licenses and badges. Access to computers and data has traditionally been authenticated through user-selected pass-words. More recently, cryptographic mecha-nisms and biometric techniques have been applied to physical and computer security, replacing or supplementing the traditional credentials. We will work to enable government and industry to be able to build secure, interoperable applications with high-assurance products that implement needed cryptographic security functionality. This will include the ongoing development of cryptographic standards and testing methods, developing methods for securing government applications with cryptography, further developing key management guidelines and schemes and the updating and creation of new modes of operation for use with cryptographic algorithms. The Bronze Medal Award is the highest honorary recognition available for Institute presentation. The award, approved by the Director, recognizes work that has resulted in more effective and efficient management systems as well as the demonstration of unusual initia-tive or creative ability in the development and improvement of methods and procedures. It also is given for significant contribution affecting major programs, scientific accomplishment within the Institute, and superior performance of assigned tasks for at least five consecutive years.

for their efforts in providing standards and guidelines in support of Federal Information Security Programs and improving the management and technical processes that are essential to successful information security program imple-mentation. Their work has been key in advancing overall security management and implementation strategy govern-ment-wide, nationally, and internationally, resulting in increased protection of information assets and supporting information technology infrastructures needed to provide critical public service.

original_blocks.html: Vendors of cryptographic modules and algorithms use independent, private-sector testing laboratories accredited as Cryptographic Module Testing (CMT) laboratories by the National Voluntary Laboratory Accreditation Program (NVLAP), to have their cryptographic modules tested by the Cryptographic Module Validation Program (CMVP) and their cryptographic algorithms validated by the Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program (CAVP). The CMVP and the CAVP are collaborative programs involving NIST’s Computer Security Division (CSD) and the Communication Security Establishment (CSE) of the Government of Canada that provide Federal agencies – in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. – with confidence that a validated cryptographic module meets a claimed level of security and that a validated cryptographic algorithm has been implemented correctly. The CMVP validates modules used in a wide variety of products including secure Internet browsers, secure radios, SmartCards, space based communications, tokens and products supporting Public Key Infrastructure and electronic commerce. One module may be used in several products so that a small number of modules may account for hundreds of products. Likewise, the CAVP validates cryptographic algorithms that may be housed in a single or multiple cryptographic modules. To give a sense of the quality improvement that both the CMVP and the CAVP achieve, consider that our statistics from the testing laboratories show that out of the first 200 modules tested, 48 percent of the cryptographic modules and 27 percent of the cryptographic algorithms brought in for voluntary testing had security flaws that were corrected during testing. In other words, without this program, the Federal government would have had only a 50-50 chance of buying correctly implemented cryptography. To date, over 585 certificates have been issued, which represents almost 1,000 validated modules by the CMVP. These modules have been developed by over 125 international vendors. Approximately 110 of these certificates were issued during 2005. Likewise, approximately 1,944 certificates have been issued for validated cryptographic algorithms.

original_blocks.html: A wide range of mechanisms is employed to authenticate identity, leveraging many different classes of identification identity credentials. For physical access, individual identity has traditionally been authenticated by use of paper credentials, such as driver’s licenses and badges. Access to computers and data has traditionally been authenticated through user-selected passwords. More recently, cryptographic mechanisms and biometric techniques have been applied to physical and computer security, replacing or supplementing the traditional credentials. The strength of the authentication that is achieved varies, depending upon the type of credential, the process used to issue the credential, and the authentication mechanism used to validate the credential.

original_blocks.html: The most common type of quantum key distribution uses a scheme developed by Bennett and Brassard (known as BB84), in which polarized photons are sent between the communicating parties and used to develop the shared key. The BB84 protocol has been studied extensively, and has been shown to be secure if implementations preserve assumptions regarding physical properties of the system. Many varieties of the BB84 scheme have been developed, and other forms of quantum key distribution have been proposed as well.

original_blocks.html: Biometric technologies consist of automated methods of identifying a person or verifying the identity of a person based upon recognition of a physiological or a behavioral characteristic. Consumers need biometric-based high-performance, interoperable (standards-based) systems developed in a timely fashion. In the absence of timely open systems standards developments, migration from proprietary systems to open-systems standard-based solutions is usually more difficult and expensive. Therefore, standards are the cornerstone of our biometrics program. Deploying new information technology systems for homeland security and for preventing ID theft require both national and international consensus standards for biometrics. We are responding to government and market requirements for open-system standards by accelerating development of formal national and international biometric standards and associated conformity assessments.

original_blocks.html: Internationally, we successfully supported the establishment of the International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission Joint Technical Committee 1 Subcommittee 37-Biometrics (ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 37-Biometrics). INCITS M1 is the national Technical Committee responsible for representing the U.S. in JTC1/SC 37. We provide the chairperson for these two standards bodies and manage their standards programs.We provide the chair of the national standards development efforts on biometric profiles (the Convener of the JTC 1/SC 37 Working Group responsible for the international biometric profile projects is provided by ITL). A large number of the projects within JTC 1 SC 37’s program of work were initiated by the U.S. (through INCITS M1). During 2005, JTC 1/SC 37 approved four of these standards. They specify biometric data interchange standard formats for face recognition (face image), finger minutiae, finger image and iris recognition (iris image). ISO published these standards also during 2005. Six additional standards are scheduled to be approved by JTC 1/SC 37 in the first quarter of 2006. NIST experts are also very active in the development of JTC 1/SC 37’s standards portfolio. We are involved in ongoing efforts within JTC 1/SC37 in defining a taxonomy to enable the Subcommittee to determine the issues that need to be resolved to ensure that conformance, interoperability, performance, and quality for the biometric data interchange format standards can be adequately addressed.
